40	## 2. How to execute
41	
42	0. **Merge this workplan first.** The task files assume the workplan is on the branch a task starts from. Until its pull request is merged to `main`, the integration base is the workplan branch (`origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0`); every task file sets `$BASE` by one line that tests which of the two holds the workplan, and gates and measures against it. A task started from a `main` that lacks the workplan would diff the whole workplan: the pilots showed it.
43	1. **One task, one session, one pull request.** Pick the next task by section 4 or 5. Open its file. Read `CLAUDE.md`. Do exactly what the file says, in its order: preconditions, evidence, change, sweep, verification, commit, adversarial pass, pull request last.
44	2. **One pull request merges at a time** (the prior workplan's rule WR-1: `grep -n "WR-1" workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md`). Branches may be prepared side by side; each later one takes the merged predecessor with `git merge origin/main` and derives its migration number again. Merging is the owner's act unless the owner has said otherwise; an executor does not merge its own pull request and does not watch it (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
45	3. **Tooling before research, never together** (CLAUDE.md rule 10). A research task starts only when the tooling it names is on `main`.
46	4. **A task that is `NOT FOR SONNET`** waits for the Fable implementation agent (design) or an Opus-class session (judgment), as its first line says. The owner authorised the Fable agent to "design, author, curate, orchestrate, delete as required" for code, schema, scripts, checks and skills (`grep -n -F "design, author, curate, orchestrate" references/project-standards.md`); doctrine stays with the owner.
47	5. **When a task stops**, it reports what it ran, what it saw and what it expected, and changes nothing further. A stop is a result, not a failure. Do not work around it.
48	5a. **The first execution of an unpiloted task is its pilot.** All but three of the task files have never been executed (section 12 says which, by command). The executor of each ends the pull request body with a heading "Task-file defects" listing what in the file was wrong, missing or ambiguous, even when the change succeeded, so the files that follow can be corrected.
49	6. **When the ground has moved** (a task's evidence command no longer gives the output the file states), the task stops. Either the defect is already fixed, or an earlier merge changed the facts; the orchestrating session re-reads the task against `main` before anyone resumes it.

241	## 7. Three tracks across the waves
242	
243	The measurements behind this section are in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` §9. **What counts as hard-coded** was sharpened by the owner on 2026-11-12: "we can set a rule for synthesis to translate, which isn't hardcoding necessarily" (`grep -n -F "isn't hardcoding necessarily" references/project-standards.md`). So: a behaviour declared **once** as a rule, in a stated place (a column's CHECK, a table, the pipeline contract, the check registry, one named constant), and read from there, is **not** hard-coding. A literal, a fixed list or a branch on a name that is typed in more than one place, or typed in code where a table, a CHECK, the contract or the registry already holds it, **is**. The word "necessarily" leaves the line open and the reading is the audit's. A dead end is a row, state, path, stage or refusal with no sanctioned way onward, back or out (also the audit's reading). The measures below therefore ask two things of a rule: that it is declared once, and that its values are not typed again elsewhere. They do not flag a rule for existing.
244	
245	```
246	for r in NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS QUANTITY_CLAIM_TYPES NOTATION_FAMILIES RULE_VERSION JurisdictionCode; do printf '%s declared %s time(s)\n' $r "$(git grep -n -E "^\s*(class )?$r\b\s*(=|\()" -- scripts schemas | wc -l)"; done   # each 0 or 1
247	git grep -n -e "'functional_axis'" -e '"functional_axis"' -- scripts schemas ':(exclude)scripts/tests' ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'   # a rule's values typed as a literal outside its home: none today; after T-010, one line, in dbcore
248	```

764	## 13. Delegated resolutions, the independent check, and the fold (2026-11-12)
765	
766	**What happened.** The owner delegated twenty register decisions to an Opus-class model (`grep -n -F "I guess opus can do it" references/project-standards.md`). The model resolved nineteen and referred OD-10 back (`DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md`). A second, independent Opus-class instance checked the four the delegation names (`DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md`): OD-01, OD-02 and OD-12 confirmed with corrections; OD-14 referred back. The corrections are appended to the ledger and marked in the resolutions file; OD-14 is withdrawn. Eighteen delegated resolutions stand.
767	
768	**The gate every task now uses** (`grep -n -F "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution" references/project-standards.md`). The ledger carries, per decision, a status line `OD-NN STATUS:` and, for a delegated resolution, a check line `OD-NN CHECK:`; the last of each wins. A decision is OPEN for a task only when its status is `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`, or `RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION` with its check `not required`, `confirmed` or `confirmed with corrections applied`. A task that needs the owner's words opens only on the first. Run for every decision:
769	
770	```
771	gate(){ s=$(grep -F "$1 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); c=$(grep -F "$1 CHECK:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1); case "$s" in *"ANSWERED BY THE OWNER"*) echo "$1 OPEN (owner)";; *"RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION"*) case "$c" in *"not required"*|*confirmed*) echo "$1 OPEN (delegated; ${c#*CHECK: })";; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (check: ${c:-none})";; esac;; *) echo "$1 CLOSED (${s:-no status line})";; esac; }
772	for n in $(grep -o -E '^### OD-[0-9]+' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md | cut -c5-); do gate $n; done
773	```

5269	ACTION: (1) Treat finding equivalencies, adjacencies, similarities and commonalities as synthesis's duty, to be done on demand and not only in a planned batch. (2) Record each relation as a pointer between existing rows and copy no fact (rule 5). (3) Leave the mechanism to the audit's improvement programme and the owner. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.

The judgment of worth is Fable's.
5280	
5281	**What it does not decide.** It does not relax the rules on how a database row gets in, and it does not make a fixture real. [ASSUMPTION: "retain" covers records (logs, findings, scripts, plans) and, for the database, only rows that are real research, entered by migration. Rows the script labels `STRESS-FIXTURE` exercised a code path and are not research; they are not retained as data. 5288	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (fifth) — the overall code is efficient, centralized and clean
5289	
5290	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5291	
5292	> "ensure the overall code is efficient and centralized and clean"
5293	
5294	**What this records.** A standing requirement on the code as a whole: efficient (no avoidable cost in time or in repeated work), centralized (one home for each rule, vocabulary, function and fact, so a change is made once), and clean (no dead, duplicated or contradictory apparatus). It extends and does not replace the 2026-10-12 and 2026-11-06 statements on minimising code and the rule-5 and rule-8 doctrine of one home per fact.
5295	
5296	**What it does not decide.** Which duplications to remove first, whether a large module is split, and what counts as "efficient" for each tool are open and belong to the audit's improvement programme. A cleanup is a change to code and is held to the same rules as any: behaviour-preserving unless a defect is being fixed, callers swept (rule 4), tooling apart from research rows (rule 10), and proven by a test that could go red. [ASSUMPTION: "overall code" is read as the scripts, schemas, checks, skills and hooks, not the guidebook's prose or data.]
5297	
5298	CONDITION: any session adding, moving, merging or deleting code, or asked whether a piece of code is redundant, duplicated or in the wrong place.
5299	ACTION: (1) Prefer one home per rule, vocabulary or function, and point to it rather than copy it. (2) Delete dead and duplicated code on evidence. (3) Measure efficiency before changing it. (4) Preserve behaviour under a refactor and prove it with a before-and-after comparison. (5) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5300	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
5301	
5302	
5303	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (sixth) — the pipeline must be flexible
5304	
5305	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5306	
5307	> "pipeline must be flexible"
5308	
5309	**What this records.** A standing property required of the pipeline as a whole, beside the objectives of the first statement of the day (any direction, any stage, dynamic, many languages and jurisdictions) and the fifth (efficient, centralized, clean). It is stated without a gloss.
5310	
5311	**What it does not decide.** What flexibility means in practice (a stage, a parameter, a language, a jurisdiction, a vocabulary or a run shape added or changed without editing code; a run entered, left or repeated at any point; a rule changed in one place) and where it must give way to a gate that holds a line are open. The tension with the derive-not-curate and one-home rules, and with gates that refuse, is for the audit's improvement programme to state; this entry resolves none of it. [ASSUMPTION: "flexible" is read as adaptable by data and configuration at the points the owner has named, not as the loosening of any refusal the project holds on purpose.]
5312	
5313	CONDITION: any session adding a fixed list, an enum, a hard-coded order or a one-shape run to the pipeline, or weighing a gate against the need to adapt.
5314	ACTION: (1) Prefer a change that is made by data or in one place over one that edits code in several. (2) Do not bake a stage, language, jurisdiction or run shape into code where the schema or a single registry can hold it. (3) Keep the refusals the project holds on purpose. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5315	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
5316	
5317	
5318	## Owner statements 2026-11-12 (seventh) — flexible means no hard-coded behaviours and no dead ends
5319	
5320	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), within minutes of the sixth statement and glossing it, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim, in the order sent:
5321	
5322	> "and that means pipeline must not have hard coded behaviours"
5323	
5324	> "or dead ends or whatever"
5325	
5326	**What this records.** The owner's gloss on "the pipeline must be flexible": the pipeline is to carry no hard-coded behaviours and no dead ends, "or whatever" of that kind. This supplies the meaning the sixth statement left open; the [ASSUMPTION] in the sixth entry about the reading of "flexible" is superseded by this gloss on that point only.
5327	
5328	**What it does not decide.** What counts as a hard-coded behaviour (a literal, a fixed list, a fixed order, a branch on a name) as against a rule held once in a registry, a column CHECK or a contract; what counts as a dead end (a state, a row, a path, a refusal or a stage with no way onward, back or out); and the "whatever" are open and belong to the audit's improvement programme. Deliberate refusals the project holds on purpose (`CLAUDE.md` §4) are not hard-coded behaviours in this sense unless the owner says so. [ASSUMPTION: "dead end" covers a reader's, a run's and a record's: a path that cannot continue or return, a row that cannot be ended or corrected, a refusal that does not say what to do next, a stage with no outbound or inbound route.]
5329	
5330	CONDITION: any session adding a fixed list, literal, order, name-branch or one-way state to the pipeline, or finding a path, row, stage or refusal that leads nowhere.
5331	ACTION: (1) Hold each rule once, in the schema, a registry or the contract, and read it from there. (2) Treat a path, row, state or refusal that leads nowhere as a defect to record and remove. (3) Keep deliberate refusals. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5332	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statements, quoted above.
5333	
5334	
5335	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (eighth) — a spelled-out number is translated into a numeral and unit; the untranslated wording may be kept as provenance
5336	
5337	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), in answer to the pilot of task T-008 (a claimed number checked as a number), which showed that a spelled-out `claimed_value` (Dutch "vijf", Finnish "viisi prosenttia") could not be filed under a check that reads numerals. Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim, the two phrases being the pilot's examples:
5338	
5339	> "\"vijf\" or \"viisi prosenttia\"
5340	>
5341	> lol just translate these into numbers/units as applicable. you can have an untranslated column for provenance if you want"
5342	
5343	**What this decides.**
5344	1. **A number written in words is translated into a numeral, and a unit where there is one,** at extraction. `claimed_value` and `claimed_unit` hold the numeral and the unit ("vijf" becomes 5; "viisi prosenttia" becomes 5 and %). The check that a claimed number is a number therefore applies to every row, and no row needs an exemption for being spelled out.
5345	2. **The wording as the source gave it may be kept in its own column,** so the translation can be seen against what it translates. The owner leaves the column to the implementer ("if you want"). `claim_text` still holds the verbatim quote.
5346	
5347	**What it does not decide.** The column's name, whether it is required, whether the translation is checked against the as-written wording (for example, that the wording occurs in the quote), and how the two stored rows that the pilot found (extraction 30, Dutch "vijf"; extraction 80, Finnish "viisi prosenttia") are brought into line. These belong to the task that implements it. This supplies the answer to GAP-056 on the point of how a spelled-out value is filed; it does not close the gap's other parts.
5348	
5349	CONDITION: any session extracting a figure a source writes in words, or changing the check on claimed values.
5350	ACTION: (1) Enter the numeral and unit as `claimed_value` and `claimed_unit`. (2) Keep the source's own wording as provenance in a column of its own where it differs from the numeral. (3) Do not exempt a row from the number check for being spelled out. (4) Do not back-translate or invent: the translation is of what the quote says.
5351	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
5352	
5353	
5354	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (ninth) — everything non-English is translated, probably at synthesis, or wherever it is needed
5355	
5356	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), directly after the eighth statement (spelled-out numbers translated into numerals and units), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5357	
5358	> "probably at synthesis or whatever we need to actually translate everything"
5359	
5360	**What this records.** The text the pipeline holds in other languages (quotations, terms, clauses, titles) is to be translated, all of it, so that it can be compared and discussed together. The owner's view of where is "probably at synthesis", and "or whatever we need": the stage is not fixed in advance, and translation is available wherever a stage needs it. Read with the eighth statement, a number is translated at extraction because the number check needs a numeral there; the rest is translated when and where it is needed, probably at synthesis.
5361	
5362	**What it does not decide.** Which stage owns translation by default, who or what translates (a person, a model, a tool) and at what class, how a translation is marked so it is never taken for the source's own words, whether a translation is reviewed, and which language is translated into (the language of a page: OD-02). It narrows OD-02 on one point only: that quotations may be translated. It does not relax the rule that a model's wording is never presented as a source's term (OR-17, E1), or the 2026-11-06 statements that English is not the pivot that decides which concepts exist (the sixth and eighth statements of that date). [ASSUMPTION: "translate everything" is read as a standing capability of the pipeline, held apart from the source text and pointing at it, not as the replacement of the source text by its translation.]
5363	
5364	CONDITION: any session translating, or deciding where translation happens, or presenting a translated quotation, term or clause.
5365	ACTION: (1) Treat translation as a capability to be called at the stage that needs it, not as a step fixed in one stage. (2) Keep the untranslated text and attach the translation to it by pointer, marked as a translation with its translator. (3) Never present a translation as the source's own wording. (4) Leave the default stage, the translator's class and the target language to the audit's programme and the owner. (5) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5366	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
5367	
5368	
5369	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (tenth) — a rule that synthesis translates is not necessarily hard-coding
5370	
5371	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), directly after the ninth statement (everything non-English is translated, probably at synthesis), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5372	
5373	> "we can set a rule for synthesis to translate, which isn't hardcoding necessarily"
5374	
5375	**What this records.** Synthesis may be given a rule to translate, and a rule of that kind is not, of itself, a hard-coded behaviour in the sense of the seventh statement. It is a gloss on the line between the two: a behaviour held once, as a stated rule that can be read and changed in one place, is permitted; a behaviour fixed as a literal or a branch scattered through code is not.
5376	
5377	**What it does not decide.** Where the rule is held (the pipeline contract, the check registry, a configuration table), how it is read, and whether the owner or the implementer may change it. The "necessarily" leaves cases open: a rule can still be hard-coding if it is buried in code or restated in several places. It does not make translation exclusive to synthesis (ninth statement: wherever it is needed). [ASSUMPTION: the sentence is read as setting synthesis as the default stage for translation by a rule held in one place that other stages can override or call, not as fixing translation to synthesis alone.]
5378	
5379	CONDITION: any session placing translation, or any other default behaviour, in a stage, or judging whether a stated rule is hard-coding.
5380	ACTION: (1) Hold a default behaviour, including "synthesis translates", as a rule in one stated place and read it from there. (2) Do not scatter it as a literal or a name-branch in code. (3) Keep the capability callable from other stages. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5381	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.

## 3. Owner definitions and directives (authoritative; from the owner in chat, 2026-10-29/30)

- **Best practice** = the best way to do something for the intended group. It is NOT the most common or most agreed value.
  The **gentlest / most accommodating value found in practice IS best practice**; no academic study is required. The Guidebook
  takes no positions. Do not highlight the steepest slope a code allows. (1:20 is gentler than Germany's ~1:16.7.)
- **Provisional** is a stage: the source must be re-read and the information confirmed. **Covered** = the listed source was read,
  extracted AND verified. At the time of writing, 0 readings were verified.
- **Scope of jurisdictions**: P1+P2+P3 only: US UK AU CA DE NO SE ISO EU; FR CH NL DK FI BE IE ES IT PT; JP SG NZ KR CN. Major
  identified countries only on the page.
- **Current editions only**; no history. T4-T6 values (e.g. 1:12) are accepted as baselines; do not hunt for their research.
  Tier numbering: `governance/tier-system.md` (2026-05-25).
- **Methodology**: the rigor belongs in synthesis, adjudication and specification, not evidence collection.
- **Evidence is binary**: recorded in the library or not. No "outside the library".
- **Item pages and the book's specifications are the same idea**: the correct way to design something.
- **Pages should render directly from the database** (matches R1/LED-103).
- **Two lenses**: an AUDIENCE lens (designer, disabled person, OT, policymaker) and a DISABILITY lens (population, ICF code,
  access need). Only the disability lens was built before.
- **Page design requirements** (full list in `reports/spec-page-design-requirements-2026-10-29.md`): controls above information;
  master comparison table with the standard's name as a small italic line under each row; value click opens detail; no "Not set"
  rows; jurisdictions alphabetical; evidence alphabetical by last name, grouped by lens; filters collapsed with pills only after a
  lens click; Swiss-grid look, one sans typeface, four sizes, no AI tropes; unit selector; APA references that open a popup with
  "cited on" lists; ●/○ evidence markers mandatory; WCAG 2.2 AA mandatory and wins over aesthetics; navigation legibility
  must not be sacrificed to minimalism. **Never self-certify accessibility.**
- **Owner hypothesis on E-03**: the problem is the lack of a rest landing, not the slope. The owner approved making rest-landing
  spacing a second headline parameter (best-practice value found so far: Germany 6 m, provisional, secondary source).
- **Persona questions the page must answer**: can an architect find the values; a policy writer find precedents and code bodies;
  a therapist/researcher find evidence; a person with a disability navigate the page.
- **Workflow**: PRs are allowed; the owner only objects to needless GitHub pinging (CLAUDE.md rule 9: open the PR once, last;
  unsubscribe immediately; do not poll). Commit and push only when asked.

**OD-2** (`decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md` §9) recorded a drafted
bucket fill order as "Ratify as drafted, noting the bucket 4/5 split is authored, not the owner's
words," but left it formally OPEN ("decisions OD-2 through OD-12 are still open; nothing gated
behind them is executed"). Batch 21 (2026-09-28) admitted Uganda — a jurisdiction in neither the
bucket scheme nor `governance/jurisdiction-philosophy.md`'s 24-canonical list — without consulting
either. The owner, live in the batch-22 orientation conversation, corrected this on contact (rule 0)
and gave a standing order:

> "Uganda ... is not a great country to hone in on." / "Please focus on the tiers 1 and 2
> countries" / "Uganda is not part of the 24 jurisdiction list" / "Standing order: do not research
> from countries other than Bucket 1 and Bucket 2 for any slug until those buckets are
> categorically exhausted."

**RULE: for every slug, research jurisdiction scope is Bucket 1 and Bucket 2 ONLY, until both are
categorically exhausted for that slug** (`workplan/2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md:420-424`,
membership below) — not merely for batch 22, and not merely for the ramp-gradient slug batch 21 and
22 work. "Categorically exhausted" means a search-coverage record (SEARCHED/THIN/NO-DATA, per the
per-jurisdiction tier-coverage convention `references/project-standards.md:121` already requires)
exists for every bucket-1 and bucket-2 jurisdiction against the slug's parameters, not merely that
some bucket-1/2 evidence has been found. Only once that is true for a slug may a session reach past
bucket 2 for that slug. This is narrower than OD-2's own draft (which scoped the buckets to a named
item set for scale-out) — this ruling applies the bucket-1/2 floor to every slug, and does not by
itself ratify buckets 4/5 or resolve the fill order beyond bucket 2.

**Bucket membership, derived from the one citation, never re-typed:**

**What this does.** With these, all six decisions the workplan says gate building are answered.

1. **OR-8.** Yes: exhaustion is judged per parameter, per bucket member, with the bucket list entered once as a table (T-6b steps 4 and 5). The owner's condition is on what a bucket member is: a jurisdiction together with its associated language, never the jurisdiction alone. [ASSUMPTION: "associated language" means the pairs `lang_jur_map` already records, whose key is language by jurisdiction, so a jurisdiction with several associated languages is several bucket members, and the bucket table points at those pairs with an approval reference on each row and does not restate the languages (rule 5).] Which pairs belong to buckets 1 and 2 is not settled here: the 2026-09-28 ruling names the buckets' jurisdictions, and T-6b proposes the pairs for the owner's approval.
2. **OR-1b.** The prompt's recommended option: a figure tagged with the identity code ALL reaches only a determination whose identity is ALL. T-3's predicate gets no clause for it.
3. **OR-4.** The prompt's recommended option: within T1, Co-1, T2 and Co-2 the most accommodating value wins, whichever of them stated it. The 2026-07-21 rule as the engine extends it is unchanged, and no composition rule has to be stated. It governs differing figures that can all be met; claims that cannot all hold are OR-6's. [ASSUMPTION: OR-5 applies first, so a Co-1 figure whose source is not academically sound is out of the numeric bound before this rule picks.]
4. **OR-6b.** The prompt's recommended option: anchoring floors that differ but can all be met (the report's example is at least 900 and at least 1500) are not divergent. The spread is printed in the value note, and T-4 step 2 does not mark them divergent, so a cell with several such sources needs no synthesis approach.
5. **OR-7.** The prompt's recommended option: a determination resting only on a regulation (T6, `code_floor_only = 1`) appears in the best-practice view, flagged with the empty circle (○), the weak marker that `governance/tier-system.md` already gives a T6 code floor. T-5 step 2 drops the `code_floor_only = 0` filter from the view. Option A, as tier-system section 8 and the architecture document line 121 ratify it, is confirmed, so no ratified text changes.
6. **OR-9.** The prompt's recommended option: no search indices are named yet, so T-6 step 6 (a table of search indices) is not built and coverage is not measured by index.
7. **OR-10.** Yes: the engine composes across exact linear units (inches and feet with millimetres and metres), converts, and shows both, the converted figure rounded to the nearest quarter inch or 5 mm. This amends ACTION (4) of "Owner ruling 2026-09-17 — PRESENT BOTH notations", which kept units apart, for exact linear units (a mark is placed at that ACTION line). Its ACTION (3), never to round a derived figure into the position of a stated figure, still holds. [ASSUMPTION: the rounding is of what is shown beside the source's own figure, and the stored bound stays exact, as T-1 step 9 reads `('36','in','>=')` as the exact fraction of a millimetre. Which way a rounded minimum or maximum moves is put to the owner as OR-10b.]
8. **OR-11a.** The prompt's recommended option: an extraction marked `verified` requires a recorded full-scope `source_scans` reading that covers the row's parameter. T-1 step 10 is built, and the renderer prints the status of each row. No ratified text changes.
9. **OR-11b.** The prompt's recommended option: a figure read in full but still `preliminary` may set a published value, flagged. No engine change, and the renderer (T-5) shows the flag. [ASSUMPTION: "for follow up" asks that the flag say the figure still awaits review; it does not by itself raise a follow-up record for each figure.]
10. **OR-12a.** The prompt's recommended option: Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili, which `lang_jur_map` requires and for which the project has no aliases, are scoped out by the bucket table until buckets 1 and 2 are exhausted, so building their aliases is not research debt now. [ASSUMPTION: with OR-8's bucket member as a jurisdiction-and-language pair, their pairs are not bucket members until then.]
11. **OR-12b.** The prompt's recommended option: a model-generated alias may be used for a search if the search is flagged. The owner adds an expectation, and it is an instruction to the model: generate only terms actually in use in the jurisdiction, not word-for-word translations of English terms. That is research rule R11 (no back-translation; every alias carries its in-language source or is marked unverified) applied to model-generated aliases. [ASSUMPTION: no stricter gate is ruled, such as requiring an in-language source before the alias is used; the flag says the alias is model-generated and not yet attested by a retrieved source. `python3 scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py` lists them.]
12. **OR-13.** The prompt's recommended option: the list of quantities (parameters) is seeded by an open-pass scan of the bucket 1 and 2 codes already held, not slug by slug. D-8 is built as written; it also needs D-3 for the open pass, T-6b for the buckets, and OR-17.
13. **OR-14.** Yes: a book page for an element (a ramp) is derived from a typed term pointer to the live determinations of its parameters, with one parameter as the degenerate case, and is never a container that rows are filed into. T-7 and D-6 are built. The owner's note places this derivation in the specifications pass: "adjudicating, deriving and synthesizing across rows of related evidence". [ASSUMPTION: that is an expectation of the pass, not only of the renderer. T-7 as proposed derives the page at read time from the parameters' determinations (a view and a renderer option); whether the specifications pass itself writes an element-level determination is put to the owner as OR-14b.]

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

content.content:
The readable text is limited. The page bodies are compressed streams I can't decode, and the bookmark titles are truncated, so some clauses may be incomplete. Where a bookmark is cut off, I've quoted only the visible part.

**1. Licence name**
- "The Classifications are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NoDerivs 3.0 IGO license (CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO" (section 1.2.2 bookmark; the URL is https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/3.0/igo/)

**2. Derivative works, adaptations, translations and mappings**
- Derivatives: "neither the Licensed Materials, nor any portion thereof, may be used for the purpose of developing or promulgating a di" (1.2.1, truncated)
- Software incorporation: "WHO does not consider incorporation of the Classifications into a software product to be an adaptation" (1.2.2)
- Data fields: "Adding data fields to Classifications concepts is permitted if such additions are clearly identified" (1.2.5)
- Mappings and translations: "Mapping or producing crosswalks between other classifications and terminologies and Classifications" and "are subject to a separate written agreement from WHO." (1.2.4)

**3. Redistribution and reproduction**
- "in data transmission and storage must include Classifications code, title and URI." (1.2.3, which concerns incorporation into software)
- The visible text does not contain a general redistribution clause for the classification content.

**4. WHO permission and contact**
- "are subject to a separate written agreement from WHO." (1.2.4, for mappings and translations)
- Suggested changes: "Suggestions for changes to the Classifications must be submitted as a proposal to the ICD-11 update platform." (1.4)
- No WHO permission contact or email appears in the readable content.

**5. Attribution wording**
- "Any mention of Classifications in published reports should include the following citation of the source:" (1.3)
- Citation text: "International Classification of Diseases, Eleventh Revision (ICD-11), World Health Organization (WHO) 2019" (1.3)

**6. Commercial vs non-commercial use**
- The readable content doesn't address commercial versus non-commercial use of the classifications. The software terms in section 2.3 grant a "royalty-free license to use and incorporate the Classifications Software," but they apply to software, not the classification content.

The full licence text, including any commercial-use or contact provisions in the truncated or unreadable portions, should be checked directly at the source.

content.content:
## Owner ruling 2026-09-11 — ICD-11 is the medical-lens source, at BLOCK grain, for correspondence

> **"Yes, use ICD-11."**
> **"eg MB5 series of codes discussing paralytic symptoms"**
> **"we are looking through ICD-11 for how it corresponds to our existing ICF/identities/access
> needs on a high level"**

This resolves the licensing hold recorded the same day: **DG-NON item 7 is answered — ICD-11 is the
source.** It also settles two things the adjudication had to guess, and corrects it on one.

**The grain is the BLOCK, not the entity.** MB5 is a block, and "on a high level" says so outright.
The adjudication had proposed 29 disease *entities* (6A02 autism, 8A40 MS, 8B00 stroke); that is the
wrong shape for a browsing lens and is superseded.

**The purpose is CORRESPONDENCE, not vocabulary.** The lens exists so a reader arriving with a
diagnosis reaches the functional demand the project holds. It is not a clinical nomenclature and must
not grow into one.

**THE JOIN IS DERIVABLE AND MUST STILL BE PRUNED.** ICF and ICD-11 are complementary WHO
classifications, and all 17 axes already declare ICF b-anchors, so the route is: ICD-11 block → the
ICF b-code it impairs → our axis → the identities and needs already attached. Nothing in that chain
is invented. **But it over-reaches, and the owner's own example proves it**: MB5 impairs b730 (muscle
power); b730 is declared by AX-AMB, AX-REA and AX-WHM; those axes carry nine identities including
BAR, LPA and TALL — who attach for *anthropometric* reasons, not muscle power. Run the join naively
and the map asserts that paralytic symptoms correspond to being tall. **That is the inference
D-0184 measured when it made the lens a column rather than a traversal, reappearing one hop further
out.** The route proposes candidates; judgment prunes; the pruning reason is recorded in the row's
`note` and its strength in `mapping_confidence`.

**What the lens reaches that nothing else does, as a measurement not an argument:** `AX-COG-L`
(Information-access demand, b117/b167) carries **zero** identities and is the only orphan of the
seventeen. ICD-11's intellectual-development and language blocks land there.

**AND NO CODE CAN BE VERIFIED FROM THE CONTAINER.** Measured: `id.who.int` 401 on every route, the
token endpoint 400 (OAuth2 client credentials required), the public browser a JavaScript application
whose HTML carries no codes, its search endpoint 0 bytes, and no WHO credentials in the environment.
So `icd11_verified_at` lands NULL on every row written today, which is precisely what that column
means. Free registration at `icd.who.int/icdapi` yields the credentials; set them on the remote
environment and `retrieval_log.fetch()` can persist real `codeinfo` payloads for
`add-medical --icd11-payload` to stamp from.

CONDITION: Any session writing a medical-lens row, or deriving an ICD-11 ↔ ICF correspondence.
ACTION: Work at block grain. Derive candidates through `axes.icf_b_anchors`, then PRUNE — never ship
the join's raw output. Leave `icd11_verified_at` NULL until a persisted WHO payload exists; never
write a code from recollection, which is CLAUDE.md §5(c) made worse by the payload being
unobtainable rather than merely unfetched.
DATE: 2026-09-11 — owner ruling, quoted above.
**(3) The demand count was wrong, and wrong in the direction that flattered the ruling.** "Exactly one
diagnosis named" was true of canonical `evidence_sources` and false of the corpus the same session was
building: the batch-06 scratch holds **REF-00979 Chow 2009, *"…for Young Men With Paraplegia"*** —
MB56 in its own title — and REF-00980 Sanford 1997. Two of eleven. **The demand test was already
firing and the session did not notice**, because it measured the committed table and not the work in
front of it.

**THE RULING AS CORRECTED.** The lens is populated **by correspondence from the registries we already
hold** — 17 axes and 23 populations, of which BAR, LPA, TALL, NDV, MOB, COM and ALL are identity-first
or umbrellas taking no anchor (`governance/functional-taxonomy.md:241-245`). That bounds it at roughly
**15–20 rows**: not 108, not zero. §4 of the functional taxonomy already names several anchors
(`:293` AUT, `:294` ADHD, `:304` LCOV). §8's "name what reads it" is satisfied — the reader is the
lens switch D-0170 was ruled for. On-demand growth continues **after** that, not instead of it.

**AND THE CHAPTER PREFERENCE WAS TOO BROAD.** "Chapter 21 is the right chapter" holds for motor and
pain — MB44 states b770 in WHO's own words, and MG30 Chronic pain sits there deliberately — and
**fails for sensory, cognitive and energy-limiting**, where the disease chapters hold the functional
block: `9D9` Vision impairment with its severity grades, `AB5` Disorders with hearing impairment,
`6A00` intellectual development, `8E49` postviral fatigue. **The rule is: anchor on the block whose
title states the presentation, wherever it sits.**

**Two further corrections to the record.** The eight-chapter set (06/08/09/10/11/15/21/22) was
described as "the chapters that could touch any of our 17 axes" and is falsified by `axes` itself —
AX-CHM declares b435/b440 (chapters 04, 12) and AX-CNT declares b620/b525 (chapters 13, 16). The
honest set is ~144 depth-1 blocks; the direction of error strengthens "do not mirror" and the stated
premise was still false. And **"the circulation literature is device-based" does not generalise**: 9

cat >> references/project-standards.md <<'EOF'


## Register entries 2026-11-12 — the fold's five owner questions entered as OD-31 to OD-35; OD-33 resolved under the twelfth instruction

Recorded in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), in the pass the owner's twelfth instruction of 2026-11-12 asked for (entry above), by an Opus-class model. **Nothing here is the owner's words.** The five questions the fold raised (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/FOLD-LOG.md` §2, PQ-1 to PQ-5) were not in the register (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §8), so the gate loop and the Definition of Done did not count them. They are entered under the next free ids: OD-31 (PQ-1, the part of GAP-076 the owner's answer of 2026-11-06 left hedged), OD-32 (PQ-2), OD-33 (PQ-3), OD-34 (PQ-4), OD-35 (PQ-5). The facts found and the prompt for each are in `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DECISION-CLOSURE.md`.

Applying the line the twelfth entry records as an [ASSUMPTION], four of the five are the owner's and are prepared, not resolved: OD-31 (population taxonomy, and confirming the owner's own hedged words), OD-32 (the owner's own review load), OD-34 (the reach of the owner's standing order of 2026-09-28: jurisdiction scope), OD-35 (how the owner's own decisions are read). One is resolved:

OD-33: the render table is a build product outside the database, generated from it at each build

**The resolution.** The render table of OW-1 is generated from `data/guidebook.db` at each build and is not stored in it; each row carries the hash of its inputs, read by the one staleness check that the render task names. This is the content of correction 4 to the delegated resolution of OD-12 (entry above), which the independent review required to be stated and which is already in force under that decision's gate; this entry gives it its own register id so that the owner can reverse it alone.

**What decided it.** Criterion 1: a table written into the database at every build would need a migration at every build, append-only and immutable (`CLAUDE.md` rule 3), so the database would accumulate superseded copies of rendered prose, a second home of facts (rule 5). Read from the database at build time, the page still comes "from database directly" (owner, 2026-10-30), and the 2026-08-27 rule that no committed file is a render is kept, because the product is generated and not committed. No owner ruling is overridden: the location "in the database" is recorded beside OW-1 as an [ASSUMPTION], not as the owner's words. Not reserved: it is a question of code architecture, not mission, audience, scope, licensing, trajectory or the weighing of groups.

**Reversal condition.** The owner placing the render table in the database (then a write path for it is designed first), or a measured build cost that a stored table would remove.

OD-33 STATUS: RESOLVED UNDER DELEGATION
OD-33 CHECK: not required

The check is `not required` because the substance is that of the OD-12 correction, which the independent review produced and whose check line already reads confirmed with corrections applied; nothing beyond it is decided here.

CONDITION: any session designing the render table, or asking whether rendered prose is stored in the database.
ACTION: (1) Generate the render table at build time from the database; store none of it there. (2) Carry an input hash per row, read by one named staleness check. (3) Treat OD-31, OD-32, OD-34 and OD-35 as the owner's. (4) Treat this as a resolution under the twelfth instruction's [ASSUMPTION], reversible by the owner.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — register entries and one resolution in the twelfth-instruction pass, not owner statements.


## Convention addendum 2026-11-12 — the status value for a decision the owner defers

Recorded in the same pass, as an addendum to "Convention 2026-11-12 — how a delegated resolution's standing is recorded, and when it opens a task's gate" (entry above). **A convention for reading the ledger, not an owner ruling**; the owner may replace it. The Definition of Done (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` §10, D-27) has always allowed a decision to end as "deferred by the owner", but the convention gave that no status value, so no command could find it.

**The addendum.** One further status value, `DEFERRED BY THE OWNER`, written only by the session that records the owner's quoted deferral of a register decision, in the same entry. The gate reads it as CLOSED (a deferred decision opens no task). D-27 counts it as settled for a decision that no task's gate reads.

CONDITION: any session recording the owner's deferral of a register decision.
ACTION: (1) Append the status line with the value `DEFERRED BY THE OWNER` beside the quoted deferral. (2) Never use it for a decision a task's gate reads; a deferral of such a decision leaves the task stopped.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — convention addendum, not an owner statement.
EOF

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (thirteenth) — MOB decomposes into more specific identity populations

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), while the decision about carrying the rows written under `MOB` (OD-14) was being prepared for the owner, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "MOB is more difficult than other categories in that it decomposes into more specific identity populations (e.g. prosthetics vs wheelchairs vs other mobility aids, power wheelchair vs manual wheelchair, paraplegia vs quadraplegia)"

**What this records.** The mobility identity is a family and not one population: it divides by the aid a person uses (a prosthesis, a wheelchair, other mobility aids), within wheelchairs by drive (power or manual), and by the level of impairment (paraplegia or quadriplegia, spelled by the owner "quadraplegia"). It is harder than the other identity categories because of this depth. The owner's examples are examples ("e.g."), not a closed list.

**What it does not decide.** Which of these divisions become identity codes, which stay descriptions of a study's participants or of a device (the extraction's `device_class` already holds one of them), how deep the hierarchy goes, whether the 2026-08-25 two-way split into ambulant people and wheelchair users stands as the first division or is superseded by a deeper one, and what a row written under `MOB` is carried as. These bear on OD-14 and on the population taxonomy, which is the owner's. [ASSUMPTION: the statement is a description of the domain that widens the question OD-14 asks, not an answer to it, and it does not by itself supersede the 2026-08-25 ruling.]

ACTION: (1) Treat `MOB` as a family with more than two levels of division, not as a pair. (2) Do not assume the two-way split is the whole decomposition. (3) Keep a division that describes a device or a participant's level in one home only (rule 5), and decide with the owner whether it is an identity code or a descriptor. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py — currency lives at the superseded text.
WHY THIS EXISTS (RC3, DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md section 4).
Binding text lives in more than five stores (DRs, the append-only ledger, the YAML
register, the `decisions` table, CLAUDE.md, the research contract and its SessionStart
copy, code comments, `sessions/*.md`), and a ruling superseding one of them was sometimes
left with no local mark: a reader who reaches the superseded sentence by grep meets it
with nothing saying it no longer holds. The fix is not a currency INDEX — that would be
the next store rule 5 forbids — it is a pointer at the text itself, anchored on quotes
that occur exactly once at both ends, checked with plain file I/O so `.ignore` cannot
hide the target (owner rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`, which `.ignore` hides
from ripgrep and the Grep tool).
THE GRAMMAR, read from the ledger and from any DR using the same trailer:
    SUPERSEDES: <target path> :: "<verbatim quote from the target>"
      BY: references/project-standards.md :: "<verbatim quote from the superseding ruling>"
NORMALISATION (so a quote survives comment wrapping, YAML folding and Markdown
blockquotes): for each line, strip leading whitespace and one leading run of `#`, `>`,
`//` or `--`, join the lines with spaces, and collapse whitespace. Both quotes must
occur EXACTLY ONCE in their own file under this normalisation.
FAILS when: the target quote occurs 0 times (edited in place, which the append-not-edit
practice forbids) or more than once (ambiguous); the BY quote does not occur exactly
once in the ledger; or no line in the target quote's own paragraph, or in the paragraph
or blockquote immediately after it, both names SUPERSEDED or AMENDED and carries the BY
quote verbatim. `BY` is always required — `DATE:` lines in the ledger are not unique
(the most repeated closes thirteen entries), so a marker cannot be anchored on one.
EXAMINED counts `SUPERSEDES:` lines. Today there may be none in a fresh clone before the
first seed lands — that is NOTHING-IN-SCOPE, not a failure (CLAUDE.md section 5a): a
check with no subject must say so, not pass by finding nothing to check.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "scripts"))
import dbcore                                                        # noqa: E402
LEDGER = REPO_ROOT / "references" / "project-standards.md"
DR_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "decisions"
# The grammar and normalisation are ONE home, scripts/dbcore.py (rule 5): this script and
# scripts/db.py's dispose-adversarial-finding (OWNER-RULED) both anchor on the same
# quotes and must count them the same way, or a ref that passes one refuses the other.
_SUPERSEDES_RE = dbcore.LEDGER_SUPERSEDES_RE
_MARKER_WORD = re.compile(r'\b(SUPERSEDED|AMENDED)\b')
def _paragraphs(text: str):
    """[(start_line, end_line, normalised_joined_text)], blank-normalised-line delimited.
    A blockquote's blank line is often `>` alone, which normalises to "" here too, so a
    blockquote paragraph is delimited the same way as a plain-prose one.
    """
    lines = text.split("\n")

1	# Population umbrellas: does "mobility" make sense as an identity, and what should the identity lens hold?
2	
3	**Status:** advisory memo for the owner. Population taxonomy is the owner's doctrine: this memo RECOMMENDS and decides nothing. It changes no file, row, ruling or task.
4	**Written:** 2026-11-12, by a Fable-class researcher-analyst, in answer to the owner's two questions of that day and under the owner's statements "thirteenth" (MOB decomposes) and "fourteenth" ("use advocacy groups and disability ethics as a lens for grouping/sorting/taxonomy").
5	**Drift warning:** every statement about the database was read from `data/guidebook.db` on 2026-11-12 (read-only). No count is quoted as a fact to trust; each carries the command that regenerates it (section 9). Every web source was retrieved on 2026-11-12; nothing was written to the retrieval log or the database, so nothing here is an admitted source.
6	
7	**Claim marks.** VERIFIED = I retrieved the page or record and read the passage. INFERRED = my reasoning, basis stated. UNVERIFIED = I believe it but did not retrieve it; do not rely on it.
8	
9	**The unratified assumption this memo works under** (ledger, fourteenth statement): "advocacy groups" means disabled people's own organisations, the CRPD's "representative organizations", not charities or service bodies speaking for them. The CRPD Committee draws that line itself (General Comment No. 7, paras 11 and 13, section 2.1). Every organisation below is flagged where the retrieved page did not show it to be led by disabled people.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 0. Verdict
14	
15	**Q1. Does "mobility" make sense as an identity population? No.** In the sources retrieved, disabled people do not organise as "people with mobility needs". They organise across disability (Council of Canadians with Disabilities, ENIL), by condition or impairment (spinal cord injury, spina bifida and hydrocephalus, limb loss and limb difference), and by device ("all wheelchair users", United Spinal Association). "Mobility" is the name of a functional domain (ICF chapter d4, the Washington Group's walking question, CRPD Article 20 on personal mobility as a right). `MOB` conflates four different kinds of fact: a function, a set of impairments, the use of an assistive device, and a number of separate communities. The owner's decomposition is correct, but its branches are not all identities: aid type and power-versus-manual are **device** facts; paraplegia-versus-quadriplegia is an **impairment-level** fact; only some branches (limb loss and limb difference, spinal cord injury, wheelchair users) correspond to communities that organise under that name. The design parameters the project has actually researched depend on the device and its user's function, not on a community.
16	
17	**Q2. Do contemporary advocates think like this? Not in this form.** They hold several layers at once: a cross-disability political identity ("disabled people", "nothing about us without us"); specific communities named on their own terms, some of which reject the impairment frame altogether (Deaf people as a linguistic and cultural group; users and survivors of psychiatry rather than "people with mental health conditions"); device-defined constituencies whose edges are contested (ambulatory wheelchair users); and, separately, functional categories that statisticians use and that advocates treat as tools, not identities. Broad impairment umbrellas ("mobility", "neurological", "mental health") are the administrative layer, not the self-defined one.
18	
19	**Q3. What do modern ethical approaches propose?** They converge on three points and disagree on a fourth. (1) Classify the **environment's demand and the barrier**, not the person (social model, CRPD, ICF environmental factors, universal design). (2) Where people are named, **they name themselves**, through their own organisations (CRPD Art. 4.3 and General Comment No. 7, epistemic justice, disability justice's "leadership of those most impacted"). (3) Keep the **individual** in view: categories are retrieval aids, never portraits (capabilities approach, care ethics, crip critique, the project's own irreducibility principle). They disagree on (4) whether impairment-specific categories should exist at all: disability justice and the social model press toward cross-disability solidarity and warn about hierarchies of impairment; community self-definition and the capabilities approach press toward specificity. The reconciliation the evidence supports is to keep the two jobs apart: communities for **voice and provenance**, access needs / ICF / device for **design parameters**.
20	
21	**RECOMMENDATION (the owner decides).** Keep the four lens columns exactly as ruled on 2026-08-28. Change what the **identity** lens is allowed to contain: only communities that disabled people have organised and named themselves, each row carrying the organisation or ethical source it rests on as provenance (the fourteenth statement's own ACTION 2). Retire `MOB` as an identity; hold "mobility" where it already lives, as ICF d4 codes and access needs. Hold device in `device_class` and nowhere else. Hold family resemblance (the "mobility family", the "neurodivergent" coalition) as a parent relation in data, used for navigation and for finding commonality, never as the key of a determination unless the family passes the ratified design-equivalence test. Record who co-produced a source as a typed relation to a community, separately from whom a determination serves. This is option 2 with option 3's hierarchy held as data, and option 4's separation of provenance from the key (section 7).
22	
23	**Confidence.** High (about 85%) that `MOB` is not an identity and that device and impairment level are not identities. Moderate (about 70%) that restricting the identity lens to self-organised communities is the right rule. Low to moderate (about 50%) on the particular list of communities, because my sample of organisations is international-umbrella and Anglophone (Canada, United States, United Kingdom, Europe), no non-English national organisation was retrieved, and several key organisations could not be reached (section 10).
24	
25	**What would change it.** (a) Evidence that organisations *of* physically disabled people, as such, are a common form outside English (the United Kingdom's Union of the Physically Impaired Against Segregation, 1975, is one; I did not retrieve any current national federation of this kind, and I think it likely that several exist: UNVERIFIED). That would support a "physical disability" community row, though still not "mobility". 53	## 2. The lens: how disabled people's own organisations define their constituencies
54	
55	### 2.1 What counts as an organisation of disabled people
56	
57	VERIFIED from the United Nations document CRPD/C/GC/7, *General comment No. 7 (2018) on the participation of persons with disabilities, including children with disabilities, through their representative organizations, in the implementation and monitoring of the Convention*, Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, distributed 9 November 2018 (https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/3899396/files/CRPD_C_GC_7-EN.pdf):
58	
59	- Para 11: organisations of persons with disabilities "can only be those that are led, directed and governed by persons with disabilities. A clear majority of their membership should be recruited among persons with disabilities themselves."
60	- Para 11(d): "They may represent one or more constituencies based on actual or perceived impairment or can be open to membership of all persons with disabilities". Para 11(e): they "can include constituencies based on transversal identities (for example, children, women or indigenous people with disabilities) and comprise members with various impairments".
61	- Para 12 names the types: umbrella organisations (which "only speak on behalf of their member organizations" and "cannot represent individual persons with disabilities"); cross-disability organisations; self-advocacy organisations, "especially persons with intellectual disabilities"; organisations including family members, for people with intellectual disabilities, dementia and children, whose role "should be to assist and empower"; organisations of women and girls; organisations of children and young persons. Para 12(a) adds: "persons with disabilities should be able to decide for themselves which organizations they want to represent them."
62	- Para 13: they "should be distinguished from organizations 'for' persons with disabilities, which provide services and/or advocate on behalf of persons with disabilities, which, in practice, may result in a conflict of interests".
63	- Para 50 gives the Committee's own list of who must be reached. It is not a taxonomy and mixes kinds freely: women, older persons, children, "those requiring high levels of support", victims of landmines, migrants, "persons with actual or perceived psychosocial impairments, persons with intellectual disabilities, neurodiverse persons, including those with autism or dementia, persons with albinism, permanent physical impairments, chronic pain, leprosy and visual impairments and persons who are deaf, deafblind or otherwise hearing-impaired".
64	
65	Three things follow for a taxonomy. INFERRED from the paragraphs above. (i) The Committee accepts **three bases of constituency at once**: impairment ("actual or perceived"), open cross-disability membership, and transversal identity. It does not rank them. (ii) Constituency is **self-chosen**: the test is who leads and whom people choose to represent them, not which box a classifier puts them in. (iii) An umbrella speaks only for its members on agreed matters and cannot represent individuals. That is the Committee's version of this project's own anti-umbrella rule.

104	2. **Where physically disabled people organise, they use one of four bases.** VERIFIED from rows 11 to 18. Cross-disability (CCD, ENIL). 113	### 3.1 What "mobility" is
114	
115	"Mobility" names an **activity domain**. VERIFIED in the project's own `identity_icf_map`: every ICF code mapped to `MOB` is a d-code (activities), and the mechanism text is "ambulation, balance, transfer, wheelchair use", four different things. VERIFIED from the United Nations text of CRPD Article 20: "personal mobility" is a right to be secured, with access to "mobility aids, devices and assistive technologies", not a class of person.

150	
151	**(a) Cross-disability political identity.** VERIFIED. UPIAS (1975): "it is society which disables physically impaired people.
